newsitem.title: USA: Hong Kong businessman bailed out Republicans - Time.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong businessman bailed out Republicans - Time.

text.p: A Hong Kong businessman helped the Republican Party free up money to buy TV ads in the crucial final days of the 1994 and 1996 political campaigns, Time magazine reported on Saturday.
The magazine reported that the businessman, Ambrous Tung Young, bailed out the party in 1994 with a $2.2 million loan guarantee and in 1996 by absorbing a $500,000 loss.

In both cases the bail-outs involved the nonprofit National Policy Forum, a think tank headed by Republican chairman Haley Barbour and a source of money for the 1994 and 1996 election campaigns, the magazine said in its latest edition due out on Monday.
Barbour on Saturday denied any wrongdoing by the Republican Party, noting that Young was a U.S. citizen.
"Barbour personally escorted Young around Washington, introducing him to (Republican presidential candidate) Bob Dole and House Speaker Newt Gingrich," the magazine reported.
Young was raised in Taiwan and has a U.S.-based company called Young Bros. Development-USA. The company owns an apartment in Washington D.C., the magazine said.
Barbour told reporters Young had been "a long-time Republican Party contributor," adding that Young Brothers Development also contributed to the party and the think tank.
"Before I was chairman they were generous donors and they were while I was there," he said.

Two congressional committees are investigating reports that Democratic fund-raisers raised money illegally or improperly from foreign sources and Republicans have been calling for a special prosecutor to investigate Democratic fund raising.
